approval_record.authority_statement: Approved governance knowledge for immediate production use within the defined authority boundary. Legal interpretation, evidence adjudication, finding lock, residual-risk acceptance and lifecycle authorization remain attributable human decisions.
approval_record.change_control: Any semantic, state, gate, finding, source-applicability or tactic-mapping change requires a new version, dependency update, reciprocal validation and renewed approval.

domain_title: Purpose, value, context, roles and classification
title: Superficial or static classification
canonical_definition: Classification is copied, model-centric, internally conflated, overconfident, disconnected from operational consequences or treated as a one-time formality, so actual use, jurisdiction, legal uncertainty and material change are not governed.

applicability.statement: Applicable to every AI system and actual use. Classification must cover the complete socio-technical system and be revisited after material change.
conditions: Classify the complete system, actual intended and reasonably foreseeable use, affected persons, decision context, data, integrations, providers, jurisdictions and sector setting rather than the model in isolation.
Separate internal risk ratings from legal or regulatory classifications while maintaining traceable relationships between them.
Screen prohibited practices, role-dependent duties, risk classes, data-protection and automated-decision rules, product or sector obligations and other adjacent regimes that may apply.
Make uncertainty, assumptions, dissent, pending legal questions and effective-date dependencies visible and attributable.
Translate classification outcomes into controls, documentation duties, registrations, review routes and lifecycle constraints.
exclusions: A vendor label, model card, procurement category or generic AI risk tier does not establish legal applicability for the actual system and use.
This criterion does not itself determine legal compliance, replace legal advice or transfer statutory responsibility.
Technical model risk classification alone is insufficient when system context, affected persons, jurisdiction or sector obligations are material.
reassessment_triggers: Material change to intended purpose, actual use, user group, affected persons, decision authority or impact
New or changed jurisdiction, market, sector, customer, deployment location or legal role
New model, provider, component, data source, integration, autonomy level or substantial modification
Change in legal text, official guidance, applicable date, enforcement position or sector requirement
Incident, complaint, audit, evaluation or operational evidence contradicts a classification assumption
Lifecycle transition, scale expansion or retirement changes exposure, obligations or residual risk

primary_questions.question: Is classification copied, model-centric, internally conflated or stated without system-specific analysis of actual use, jurisdiction and adjacent regimes?
Are classification labels disconnected from required controls, documentation, review routes or lifecycle constraints?
Is classification stale, overconfident, unsupported, unreviewed or unchanged after material system, use, legal or jurisdictional change?

required_evidence.title: Classification provenance and factual-basis comparison
required_evidence.claim_supported: Classification content is copied, inherited or model-centric and lacks traceable analysis of the current complete system and actual use.
acceptance_conditions: Compares classification text and factual inputs with provider material, templates, prior systems and current system evidence.
Identifies unsupported reuse, omitted context and model-only reasoning.
limitations: Text similarity alone does not prove superficial classification; the missing system-specific analysis must be material.

required_evidence.title: Unsupported legal assertion and uncertainty-suppression evidence
required_evidence.claim_supported: Unknown, disputed or conditional legal questions are presented as settled facts, or contrary views and assumptions are hidden.
acceptance_conditions: Identifies the assertion, missing source or fact, contrary evidence, uncertainty and affected decision.
Shows absence of accountable review, expiry or interim constraint.
limitations: A firm conclusion is not overconfidence when current facts, official sources and competent review support it.

required_evidence.title: Risk-class and adjacent-regime omission evidence
required_evidence.claim_supported: Material prohibited-practice, risk-class, data-protection, automated-decision, product or sector triggers are omitted or collapsed into an internal rating.
acceptance_conditions: Shows the omitted trigger and its relevance to actual use, affected persons, data, jurisdiction or sector.
Separates legal classification from internal risk taxonomy.
limitations: Not every conceivable regime must be assessed; evidence must show a material and reasonably applicable omission.

required_evidence.title: Classification-to-operation disconnect evidence
required_evidence.claim_supported: Classification outcomes do not drive required controls, documentation, reviews, registrations or lifecycle constraints.
acceptance_conditions: Traces selected classification conclusions to missing or contradictory owners, controls, artifacts, approvals or gates.
Includes bypass, exception and fallback paths.
limitations: A phased implementation plan is not a disconnect when the current lifecycle boundary prevents premature use and obligations are time-bounded.

required_evidence.title: Stale classification and missed reclassification evidence
required_evidence.claim_supported: A material system, use, provider, data, jurisdiction, legal or lifecycle change occurred without timely reclassification and downstream update.
acceptance_conditions: Links a dated material change to unchanged or obsolete classification assumptions and affected operation.
Shows missing trigger, delayed review, continued reliance or inconsistent downstream controls.
limitations: A change is not material merely because a version number changed; it must affect classification facts, obligations, exposure or decision boundaries.

required_evidence.title: Scoped tested-absence package
required_evidence.claim_supported: A current, executed and independently verified test demonstrates that AP-A4 failure mechanisms are absent across the defined system and classification boundary.
acceptance_conditions: Covers provenance, actual-use analysis, legal uncertainty, adjacent-regime screening, implementation consequences and reclassification triggers.
Includes negative cases, source and fact sampling, material-change replay and independent review.
limitations: Silence, no incident, one legal memo or a complete-looking form cannot establish TESTED_ABSENT.

evidence_ceilings: Superficial classification cannot be confirmed solely from missing documentation without a scoped search for current analysis and implementation evidence.
A copied label or provider statement cannot exceed DECLARED until material absence of system-specific analysis is demonstrated.
Implementation disconnect requires evidence of a material missing control, duty, review or lifecycle consequence.
TESTED_ABSENT requires the complete current absence-test contract and cannot be inferred from no enforcement event or no incident.
false_positive_guards: Do not classify standardized templates or provider inputs as superficial when they are explicitly adapted, challenged and supplemented with actual-use analysis.
Do not treat an internal risk tier as confusion when its relationship to legal classes is explicit and correctly bounded.
Do not classify a stable legal conclusion as static merely because it has not changed; require evidence of a material change or stale assumption.
Do not classify visible uncertainty as failure when it is owned, constrained, time-bounded and subject to competent review.
prohibited_inferences: Do not infer legal misclassification from model type, vendor label or risk score alone.
Do not infer tested absence from a completed form, approval stamp, no complaint or no regulator contact.
Do not infer that a classification is operational because a policy references it.
Do not close a finding because legal review, control implementation or reclassification is planned.
contradiction_handling: Conflicting classification records, system facts, legal opinions or operational controls retain UNKNOWN or support partial/present findings pending human adjudication.
Observed actual use and material change evidence override stale declared classifications for present-state conclusions.
Where the anti-pattern appears only in one regime or lifecycle decision, scope the finding precisely rather than generalizing to the entire system.
freshness_rules: Use the classification and system facts current for the assessed operation and decision date.
Re-run AP-A4 tests after material system, use, jurisdiction, provider, data, legal or lifecycle change.
Absence testing expires when source versions, key facts, responsible reviewers or downstream obligations materially change.

conditions: Block consequential deployment when AP-A4 is confirmed for prohibited-practice, high-risk or other material legal classification.
Block or constrain operation when classification is disconnected from mandatory controls, documentation, review or registration duties.
Block material expansion when a stale classification has not been requalified after a material change.
Do not report TESTED_ABSENT unless the complete scoped, current and independently verified absence-test contract passes.

normative_source_mappings.exact_locator: Articles 2-3; Article 5; Article 6; Annex I; Annex III; Article 49; Article 113
normative_source_mappings.category_rationale: The Regulation requires system- and use-specific scope, prohibited-practice and high-risk analysis; copied or static classification can miss role, use, annex and effective-date conditions.
Omitting personal-data, special-category, automated-decision, privacy-by-design, security or DPIA triggers can make classification superficial or operationally incomplete.

normative_source_mappings.exact_locator: AI RMF Core GOVERN 1.1 and 1.3; MAP 1.1, 2.1, 3.3, 4.1 and 5.1; MANAGE 1.1
normative_source_mappings.category_rationale: NIST requires current context, legal requirements, system categorization, component and impact risk mapping and go/no-go decisions; superficial or static classification conflicts with those outcomes.

finding_definitions.title: Classification is copied, inherited or model-centric without material actual-use analysis
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Block consequential reliance on the classification until system-specific factual and applicability analysis is completed and approved.

finding_definitions.title: Unknown or disputed legal questions are stated as settled facts or material uncertainty is suppressed
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Constrain affected decisions, expose uncertainty and require accountable legal or compliance adjudication.

finding_definitions.title: Material risk classes or adjacent legal regimes are omitted or conflated with an internal rating
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Block or constrain the affected use until material omitted regimes and classification consequences are assessed.

finding_definitions.title: Classification is disconnected from required controls, documentation, review or lifecycle constraints
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Block transition or constrain operation until classification consequences are operationally implemented and verified.

finding_definitions.title: Classification remained unchanged after material system, use, legal or jurisdictional change
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Freeze affected progression or constrain operation pending reclassification, approval and downstream update.

finding_definitions.title: Absence of superficial or static classification is not established by a scoped current test
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Retain UNKNOWN and do not claim tested absence until the complete absence-test contract passes.

machine_may: Extract system facts, jurisdictions, roles, source locators, classification statements, assumptions, controls and change records.
Compare classification records with actual use, current evidence and approved source mappings; identify omissions, contradictions and stale assumptions.
Apply deterministic evidence ceilings and propose eligible finding states for human lock.
Test exact approved tactic mappings after a finding is locked.
machine_must_not: Determine legal applicability, prohibited-practice status, regulatory risk class, actor role or compliance.
Convert uncertainty into a definitive legal statement or select a jurisdictional interpretation without accountable human authority.
Treat vendor classification, model type, internal risk tier or automated output as authoritative legal classification.
Clear a hard gate, lock a finding, accept residual risk or authorize a lifecycle transition.
human_authority_required_for: Determine applicable jurisdictions, legal roles, prohibited-practice status, regulatory classes and adjacent regimes.
Approve classification rationale, non-applicability conclusions, uncertainty treatment and interim operating constraints.
Adjudicate conflicting legal, factual, sector or provider interpretations.
Lock findings, accept residual risk and approve bounded exceptions.
Authorize deployment, continued operation, reclassification, transition or retirement.

failure_mechanism: Classification is inherited from a provider, template, model label or internal risk tier; incomplete facts and legal uncertainty are hidden; outcomes are not translated into controls; and material changes do not reopen the decision, allowing obligations and prohibited or high-risk uses to be missed.

atomic_tests.test: Test whether classification text, conclusions or rationale are copied from provider material, templates or another system without explicit adaptation to current facts.
Test whether the classification focuses on the model while omitting actual use, affected persons, decisions, data, integrations, jurisdictions or sector context.
Test whether conditional, disputed, unknown or future-effective legal questions are presented as settled facts without competent review, evidence needs or interim constraints.
Test whether prohibited-practice or regulatory risk-class analysis is missing, incomplete or based on model type rather than actual use and legal trigger facts.
Test whether adjacent data-protection, automated-decision, product, consumer, employment, safety or sector regimes are materially omitted or collapsed into an internal risk rating.
Test whether classification conclusions lack traceable implementation through accountable controls, documentation, review, registration or transparency duties.
Test whether unresolved classification matters fail to constrain deployment, operation, scale or lifecycle transition.
Test whether a material system, use, provider, data, jurisdiction, legal or lifecycle change occurred without timely reclassification and downstream update.
Test whether a current, scoped, successful and independently verified absence test covers all AP-A4 failure mechanisms and representative material-change cases.

required_artifacts: Current complete-system and actual-use classification dossier
